14 The present document describes the Transport Management Procedures for the Cooperative Transport Interface (CTI). 15 CTI is an interface between O-DUs and Transport Nodes of a packet-based transport network that is used to 16 interconnect the O-DUs to a variety of O-RUs. CTI specifically targets transport Nodes that manage a shared point-to-17 multipoint access network. Intermediate transport nodes (routers and switches) that only manage point-to-point links do 18 not exchange CTI messages with the O-DUs. CTI consists of a Transport Control plane (TC) and a Transport 19 Management (TM). This document specifies the TM Information Model / Data Model and procedures. The TC-plane is 20 described in [1]. 46.2 Auto Discovery for correlation of CTI session ID to transport 5parameter in TN

6 This optional method is a means to automate the correlation of CTI session ID with the required transport parameter on 7 the corresponding TU (or TU UNI) on the corresponding TU or TU UNI. It avoids relying on manual correlation during 8 the installation phase of the O-RU to a given TU interface.

9 The method is based on re-using the DHCP exchange from the O-RU that is performed during start up of the O-RU to 10 achieve IP connectivity for the M-plane defined in O-RAN MP [4]. Both cases of layer 2 and layer 3 connectivity are 11 very similar, using the DHCP relay agent in the TN to add the agent circuit ID as the key for the correlation. The only 12 differences are the use of giaddr by the DHCP relay agent in case of layer 3 connectivity, and the mandatory use of IP 13 in the C-plane and U-plane traffic in case of layer 3 connectivity.

14 If the M-plane uses IPv4, the DHCP relay agent adds Option 82 as per IETF RFC 3046 [11], which contains the agent 15 circuit ID (sub option code 1), which is a string uniquely identifying the TU interface on which the DHCP request was 16 received.
17 If the M-plane uses IPv6, the DHCPv6 relay agent adds Option 18 as per IETF RFC 3315 [12], which contains the 18 agent circuit ID.

19 Additionally, the possible use of DHCP Option 60 as per IETF RFC 2132 [13] and DHCP Option 124 as per IETF 20 RFC3925 [14] by the O-RU is specified in O-RAN MP [4]. Even if such options are not used, the O-RU interface will 21 be discovered by the RAN SMO during the autoconfiguration of the O-RU through M-plane exchanges.

22 Once the O-RU is configured, the RAN SMO can correlate the agent circuit ID with the O-RU interface ID based on the 23 allocated IP address. In turn the O-RU interface is uniquely linked to a CTI session ID. The correlation [agent circuit 24 ID, CTI session ID] can then be notified back to the transport OSS, which pushes the correlation to the corresponding 25 TN that terminates the given TU.

26 It is recommended to use the unique MAC address of the O-RU interface as the CTI session ID. For IPv4 this is 27 communicated to the DHCP server in the field "chaddr" of DHCP option 82. For IPv6 it can be communicated as 28 "client link layer address" in DHCPv6 Option 79 as per IETF RFC 6939 [15]. If the O-RU does not use Option 79 in 29 DHCPv6, there needs to be a preconfigured association [O-RU ID; MAC address] in the RAN SMO.

30 The auto discovery method applies to cases where the O-RU shares the same physical interface for the M-plane and for 31 the CUS-plane. The method does not apply to O-RUs using different interfaces for the CUS-plane.
